I will think this through the way I always do — what did I do last year, what do the neighbors do, and what did I harvest.

Last year the wheat came out good, about 1000 jin (500 kg) per mu, and the maize about the same. Cotton was okay, not great, but the price was decent so I keep growing it. I do not change much because changing is how you lose money.

My 15 mu — I split it like I always do. I keep 10 mu for the wheat-maize rotation, that is the main food and the main income. The other 5 mu I keep for cotton because cotton brings cash and I know how to grow it for 40 years now.

For wheat, I do like old Li next door. Before planting, I put 2 bags of compound fertilizer (that 15-15-15 kind) per mu, that is about 50 kg. Then when the wheat turns green in spring, I put 1 bag of urea per mu, about 40 jin (20 kg). Better to put a little extra than have yellow wheat — yellow wheat means no grain, and no grain means no money. I use the good seed the dealer sells, the one the neighbors use. I water 4 times — before winter, green-up, jointing, and when grain is filling. The well is there, water is cheap enough. I spray 2 times — once for aphids, once for the disease on the head.

For summer maize after wheat, I plant right away, no ploughing, just put the seed in with the machine. I put 1 bag compound at planting, then about 30 jin urea when the maize is waist-high. Maize does not need so much water here, 1 time is usually enough, sometimes 2 if the rain is bad. Spray once for the borer.

For cotton on the 5 mu, cotton needs more care. I plough that land, put manure if I have it plus 2 bags compound per mu before planting. I use the Bt cotton seed, everyone uses it now, the bollworm does not bother it so much. Still I spray 5-6 times for the other bugs and the leaf trouble. Water 3 times. Cotton is tiring but I know it.
